name: Ashwall Ironblood Claimant's Colors Jacket
description:
A heavy-canvas moto-cut jacket in oxidized burgundy, worn by members of the Ironblood Shelf gang network. Back panel features hand-embroidered territorial sigils in copper wire thread — specific stitch patterns denote block, rank, and kill-count by those who know how to read them. Front lapels bear heat-pressed patch clusters: faction crest, allied crew marks, and a narrow black stripe for each year of standing.

Cuffs are raw-cut and re-stitched with salvaged industrial webbing. Most jackets show deliberate acid-bleach scoring along the left shoulder — a ritual mark applied upon initiation. No two are identical; forgeries are spotted immediately by the asymmetry of authentic hand-work.
functionality: Reinforced canvas provides mild blunt-force protection. Interior pocket sewn for blade or compact tool. Aug-compatible left sleeve has snap-out panel for chrome arm clearance.
what_it_says: I am claimed, I am known, and the Shelf knows exactly where I stand.
story_hooks: A runner finds a jacket with seven kill-stripes abandoned in a neutral zone — someone wants it found.
A Tier 3 fashion designer is caught selling 'authentic Ironblood aesthetic' knock-offs upstack; the crew wants a conversation.
A new arrival on the Shelf is offered a jacket with no patches yet — a blank slate invitation with strings attached.

physical_description.visual_profile: Heavy, imposing moto-cut jacket with a lived-in brutalist aesthetic. Oversized shoulders and squared-off silhouette read as deliberately intimidating. The oxidized burgundy base has a weathered, almost rust-toned appearance that catches light unevenly. Layered patch clusters on chest create visual weight and texture variation.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through shoulders and torso, intentionally oversized for layering and movement. Tapers slightly at waist. Cuffs sit loose and raw-edged. Designed for functional wear rather than body-hugging aesthetics.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy canvas base, aged and treated to achieve oxidized burgundy tone. Copper wire thread embroidery on back. Salvaged industrial webbing on cuffs. Heat-pressed synthetic patches.
physical_description.texture: Coarse, structured canvas with visible weave. Hand-embroidered copper sigils create raised, tactile patterns on back panel. Acid-bleach scoring visible as rough, whitened striations along shoulder. Raw-cut edges with uneven stitching reinforce hand-crafted quality.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep oxidized burgundy base with copper-thread embroidery, black patch stripes, varied crew marks in metallic and matte finishes. White acid-bleach scoring creates high-contrast ritual marks.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty brass or salvaged metal snaps down front. Industrial webbing cuff closures. No zipper—old-school button or snap design.
distinctive_features: Hand-embroidered copper-wire territorial sigils on back panel encoding block, rank, and kill-count data
Acid-bleach scored left shoulder marking initiation into crew
Chest patch cluster: faction crest, allied crew marks, and black stripe tally system for years of standing
Raw-cut, hand-stitched cuffs with salvaged industrial webbing
Intentional asymmetry and visible hand-work to prevent forgery
Oxidized burgundy patina suggesting age and street weathering
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4-5 street/sub-grade. Handmade collective craft, not commercial manufacture. Signals ungoverned gang affiliation and earned standing.
physical_description.cultural_context: Ironblood Shelf gang network member. Wearing this jacket is a direct claim to territorial control, crew loyalty, and personal combat history. The embroidered sigils and patch marks serve as a resume for those who can read gang heraldry. Forgery is a serious offense.
physical_description.condition_typical: Deliberately worn and weathered. Canvas shows fading, acid scarring, and patina. Patches may be newer or older depending on wearer's tenure. Stitching intentionally irregular to prove hand-craft authenticity. Looks lived-in and battle-marked.
